question: Point out which type of disorder best fits the following clinical description: insidious but progressive development of extravagant behavior, with an inability to meet the demands of social life and a decrease in overall performance. There is no evidence of hallucinations or delusions. "Negative" traits appear without having been preceded by clearly manifest psychotic symptoms.
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Progressive development of extravagant behavior -> Inability to meet social demands -> Decrease in overall performance -> No evidence of hallucinations or delusions -> Negative traits without preceding psychotic symptoms -> Simple schizophrenia -> 80%
enhanced_information: The clinical description provided aligns with Simple schizophrenia, characterized by insidious but progressive development of extravagant behavior, inability to meet social demands, decrease in overall performance, absence of hallucinations or delusions, and negative traits emerging without preceding psychotic symptoms. This conclusion is supported by the reasoning chain provided.
analysis: The clinical description aligns with the features of Simple schizophrenia, characterized by an insidious and progressive development of extravagant behavior, social dysfunction, decreased performance, absence of hallucinations or delusions, and negative symptoms emerging without prior psychotic symptoms. This presentation is consistent with the enhanced information provided.
